    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.
Både Timon Haugan og Henrik Kristoffersen tapte halvannet sekund til Braathen i første omgang. Begge fortsatte å skuffe i andre omgang og ble henholdsvis 18 og 19.
– Jeg kjørte i en stein, forteller Kristoffersen til TV 2.</description>

      <pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 12:48:18 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">1.18082207</guid>
      <dc:date>2026-11-15T12:48:18Z</dc:date>

        <media:title>Bilder fra TV 2: Lucas Braathen med nok en seier i Levi</media:title>

    <item>
      <title>Vind og kaos-skyting: Kirkeeide vant fellesstarten etter åtte (!) bom</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/vind-og-kaos-skyting_-kirkeeide-vant-fellesstarten-etter-atte-___-bom-1.18082184</link>
      <description>Maren Kirkeeide stakk av med seieren på kvinnenes fellesstart i skiskyting på Geilo søndag.
Lørdagens sprintsensasjon Guro Ytterhus imponerte igjen og tok andreplass 14,4 sekunder bak Kirkeeide.
Juni Arnekleiv ledet etter to fulle hus, men på tredje skyting ble det kaos. Sterk vind gjorde at flere av utøverne bommet mange ganger, og Arnekleiv røk på fire bom.
Dermed tok Karoline Knotten over teten. Men på siste skyting, så haglet skuddene utenfor blinkene nok en gang.
Og plutselig var Kirkeeide i tet etter hele åtte (!) bom. Få løpere måtte ut i flere strafferunder, men likevel holdt hun ledelsen helt til mål.
– Det var en merkelig fellesstart. Det var veldig mange som bommet. Det var tydeligvis ikke så lett som man skulle tro, sier Kirkeeide til NRK etter seieren.
Karoline Knotten tok tredjeplass.
Ingrid Landmark Tandrevold, Marthe Kråkstad Johansen, Karoline Knotten og nevnte Kirkeeide er forhåndsuttatt til verdenscupstarten i finske Kontiolahti senere i måneden. Kvinnenes tropp skal til slutt bestå av seks løpere.</description>

      <description>Tidligere idrettsutøver Birgit Skarstein sier hun er klar til å bidra dersom hun blir ordførerkandidat for Arbeiderpartiet.
Oslo Aps nominasjonskomité samlet seg fredag kveld om den tidligere parautøveren som ordførerkandidat ved kommunevalget neste høst.
Skarstein sa først nei til plassen, men endret senere mening.
– Da nominasjonskomiteen ringte tre uker senere, hadde vi fått områdd oss, og jeg kjente at jeg var veldig motivert. Heldigvis er det lov å tenke seg om, skriver hun i et innlegg på Facebook.
Den endelige avgjørelsen skal tas på nominasjonsmøtet i Samfunnssalen over Sentrum Scene 22. november.</description>

      <description>USAs transportminister Sean Duffy sier utskiftning av en kobbertråd kan være årsaken til den omfattende flystansen fredag.
Flere enn 15.000 flygninger ble forsinket eller innstilt da amerikanske luftfartsmyndigheter FAA i fire timer nektet alle fly å ta av på grunn av forstyrrelser i flykontrollen.
På en pressekonferanse lørdag sa transportminister Duffy at problemene kan ha oppstått som følge av arbeidet med å bytte ut gamle kobberkabler med fiber ved et av FAAs anlegg.
Ministeren oppgav også navnet på selskapet han mente hadde forsårsaket problemene. Hendelsen skal granskes videre.
Det er fremdeles etterslep etter fredagens problemer. Lørdag er flere enn 10.000 flygninger innstilt eller forsinket, ifølge FlightAware.</description>

      <description>Det brenner kraftig i en enebolig på en gård i Trondheimsveien i Lillestrøm.
– Det er full fyr i hele bygningen, opplyser oppdragsleder i politiet, Ronny Mangseth.
– Brannvesenet er fremme og er i gang med slukking. Det er kontroll på alle fire beboere på stedet, sier han.
Ved 17:20-tiden opplyser politiet at det fortsatt brenner i boligen, og at arbeidet med slukking vil ta tid.
En person skal ha fått i seg noe røyk.
Det skal ikke være fare for spredning til låve eller andre bygninger på gården.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke kjent hva som er årsaken til brannen, og de vil etterforske saken videre.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Solbakken overrasker – Aasgaard inn i startelleveren</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/solbakken-overrasker-_-aasgaard-inn-i-startelleveren-1.18081988</link>
      <description>Ståle Solbakken har valgt ut følgende ellever til kampen mot Wales på Ullevaal:
Egil Selvik – Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Møller Wolfe – Sander Berge, Martin Ødegaard, Thelo Aasgaard – Antonio Nusa, Erling Braut Haaland, Oscar Bobb.
– Jeg må innrømme at jeg er noe overrasket. Men da tenker vel Solbakken at han passer bedre til denne kampen enn det Patrick Berg gjør akkurat nå, sier NRK-ekspert Andrine Hegerberg om at Aasgaards inntog i startelleveren.
Han er én av fire bytter som er gjort fra elleveren som møtte Portugal i forrige nasjonsligakamp.
Leo Østigård, Andreas Schjelderup og Patrick Berg er henvist til benken, mens Fredrik Aursnes ikke er med på grunn av en skade.
Samtidig er det nok en gang Egil Selvik som skal vokte buret for Norge.
– Jeg er først og fremst stolt, men også spent. Det blir en viktig kamp for oss, så det gjelder å gi jernet. Vi har noe å revansjere, sier Selvik til TV 2.
På motsatt banehalvdel starter Wales med følgende mannskap:
Karl Darlow – Neco Williams, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Jay Dasilva – Harry Wilson, Ethan Ampadu, Liam Cullen, Daniel James – Lewis Koumas, Brennan Johnson.</description>

      <description>Den tidligere Outlaws-sjefen og countrymusikeren er død, 82 år gammel, melder VG.
Holm Hansen ledet MC-klubben Outlaws, ble dømt for handel med narkotika og våpen og ga ut countrymusikk.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/microsoft-trobbel-rammer-tusenvis-av-brukere-1.18080878</link>
      <description>Microsoft opplever tekniske problemer som rammer brukere av blant annet e-posttjenesten Outlook og Teams. Selskapet opplyser at de jobber med å løse saken.
Også andre Microsoft-produkter er berørt, blant annet SharePoint og Planner.
Årsaken er at en del av infrastrukturen opplevde «forhøyet belastning, ifølge Microsoft. Selskapet fant ut at en rekke servere var «uventet utilgjengelige».
Ifølge nettstedet Downdetector nådde problemene et høydepunkt ved 19-tiden norsk tid, med 129 476 feilmeldinger.
Ved 5.30-tiden natt til fredag har antallet feilmeldinger falt til 21 988.</description>

      <description>Informasjon om 144.249 passasjerer hos Norwegian og Widerøe er lekket i forbindelse med datainnbruddet hos den spanske IT-leverandøren Amadeus.
Det kommer fram i et brev Norwegian har sendt til Datatilsynet.
Fra før har SAS opplyst om at 350.000 av deres passasjerer er rammet.
Norwegian skriver at de fortløpende vurderer å varsle passasjerene.

CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ Independent and employee owned - local news stories, weather, sports, events and more Tue, 17 Nov 2026 23:49:49 +0000 en-CA hourly 1 https://cheknews.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/cropped-CHEK-Mark-512x512-1-200x200.png?crop=1 CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ 32 32 70014466 LeBlanc fields questions about trade negotiations with Trump administration https://cheknews.ca/leblanc-fields-questions-about-trade-negotiations-with-trump-administration-1362062/ Tue, 17 Nov 2026 23:49:48 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1362062

Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc maintained Tuesday that Prime Minister Mark Carney's version of the events leading up to the collapse of U.S. trade talks was accurate as he was questioned by members of Parliament in Ottawa.

The post LeBlanc fields questions about trade negotiations with Trump administration appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc maintained Tuesday that Prime Minister Mark Carney’s version of the events leading up to the collapse of U.S. trade talks was accurate as he was questioned by members of Parliament in Ottawa.

“The prime minister accurately described the conversations we had in those last days in Washington,” LeBlanc told MPs on the standing committee on international trade.

U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade war rapidly escalated after trade talks broke down in August, as Ottawa and Washington accused each other of pushing eleventh-hour changes.

Carney said at the time that Trump’s team wanted to restrict Canada’s ability to make trade deals with other countries, endanger Canada’s protections for language and culture, and maintain hefty tariffs on some automobiles.

United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in response that the prime minister’s description of the trade talks “goes far beyond anything we’ve discussed.”

Conservative MP Jacob Mantle questioned LeBlanc about the competing narratives. “Who is telling the truth?” he asked.

“I think the prime minister was absolutely correct to say on that last day were introduced elements that would have restricted Canada’s ability to enter into free trade agreements with other countries,” LeBlanc said.

“Certain sectors were identified by the Americans. At the end of the day it was a balance … where the prime minister concluded that that is in the sovereign interest of Canada.”

Mantle pointed to sections of the Canada-U.S.-Mexico Agreement on trade, known as CUSMA, that already bar partner countries from entering into trade agreements with non-market economies. LeBlanc replied that Mantle was assuming those conversations were about non-market economies.

Tuesday’s hearing provided no real insights into the trade talks or the current state of negotiations.

LeBlanc told the committee that he and Greer agreed not to publicly discuss details. The minister said he remains in contact with Greer and U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

A bilateral deal that benefits Canada and the United States is still possible, LeBlanc told the hearing.

The Trump administration softened its public stance toward Canada after Democrats swept this month’s midterm elections — a result that was a clear rebuke of the president’s policies, including his sweeping tariff agenda.

Democrats have indicated that ending the trade war with Canada will be a top priority when they take the majority in Congress in January. Some experts say it may be challenging for Democrats to achieve the supermajority they would need to override the president’s veto.

Observers also have said Democrats likely will only tackle one of Trump’s tariff tools — Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 — while leaving in place other duties still hammering parts of the Canadian economy.

Trump used Section 338 to hit an array of Canadian goods with 50 per cent levies. Weeks later, using the same Depression-era statute, he banned imports of other Canadian goods, including motorcycles and some alcohol and dairy products.

Democrats are expected to be much less likely to take down Trump’s separate sectoral tariffs or his 10 per cent duty linked to claims of forced labour in supply chains.

Democrats have a broad protectionist streak of their own and many of their newly elected members of Congress are not opposed to using tariffs to protect domestic industries.

At Tuesday’s hearing, Conservative MP Shuvaloy Majumdar asked Canada’s chief trade negotiator, Janice Charette, if Ottawa’s goal is still to achieve tariff-free trade.

Charette said the United States is changing its trade with every country and all of Trump’s deals have included some level of tariffs. Canada has to prepare for a world where a tariff-free arrangement may not be possible, she said.

The objective is to “get to the lowest rate of tariff on the narrowest basket of goods with the most preferential access for Canadian businesses and Canadian workers,” Charette added.

“That is the premise for the CUSMA agreement. That is what has made us so successful, so prosperous as three countries in North America, and we’d like to try and get as close back to that as possible,” she said. 

“But we do have another partner on the other side of the table and they have shown to date an unwillingness to enter into any arrangement in which there is full tariff-free trade.”

Charette and LeBlanc also fielded questions about how Canada is reaching out to Mexican colleagues as Ottawa and Mexico City continue to advocate for a renewal of the continental trade pact.

The Trump administration in July chose not to renew CUSMA. The decision triggered a rolling annual review for up to a decade, at which point the agreement will expire if the three countries cannot agree on an extension.

Carney met earlier Tuesday with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on the sidelines of an economic summit in China.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 17, 2026.

— By Kelly Geraldine Malone in Washington

]]> 1362062 Royal BC Museum apologizes to Sdahl Ḵ’awaas for systemic racism in historic ceremony on Haida Gwaii https://cheknews.ca/royal-bc-museum-apologizes-to-sdahl-%e1%b8%b5awaas-for-systemic-racism-in-historic-ceremony-on-haida-gwaii-1361940/ Tue, 17 Nov 2026 22:30:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361940

Six years after her high-profile departure, Sdahl Ḵ'awaas (Lucy Bell) has received a formal Haida traditional apology from the Royal BC Museum for experiencing systemic racism and discrimination.

The post Royal BC Museum apologizes to Sdahl Ḵ’awaas for systemic racism in historic ceremony on Haida Gwaii appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Six years after her high-profile departure, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas (Lucy Bell) has received a formal Haida traditional apology from the Royal BC Museum (RBCM) for experiencing systemic racism and discrimination.

The historic ceremony marks a significant milestone in a long battle for accountability, one that began when Sdahl Ḵ’awaas resigned from her position as head of Indigenous collections in 2020.

Uncovering truth

When Sdahl Ḵ’awaas left the institution, staff were told she was simply finishing her PhD. That narrative was false. On her final day, she set the record straight, revealing to colleagues that her departure was driven by systemic racism, a reality that former executives kept hidden.

An independent investigation later substantiated her allegations. As part of her Human Rights Tribunal filing, she asked for a public apology from the museum, bringing to light institutional attitudes she faced firsthand.

“We don’t have time to consult with First Nations. Indigenous people don’t really want their things back. It’s a conflict of interest for you to talk to the Haida about the museum. There’s no such thing as racism.” These were just some of the stories and interactions Sdahl Ḵ’awaas shared with staff during her departure party in June 2020.

The apology

After consulting with her clan, and despite initial hesitation from some, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas accepted the museum’s apology, delivered by RBCM CEO Allison Bond.

“I’m sorry that it took your courage to make that change and I am sorry that it took harm for us to be here today,” Bond said at the podium. “It shouldn’t have happened and I am sorry.”

Reflecting on the moment, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas noted the complexities of the apology. “The CEO was doing her best to be genuine and I saw that,” she said. “It’s easy to say sorry for something that you haven’t caused, so it is a little bit of an awkward situation. She is the sixth CEO since I was there.”

Bond emphasized that the apology carries institutional and personal weight.

“It isn’t just me speaking as the CEO, it has to be me as Allison, bringing forward my apology and the sincerity of the apology and understanding that this is a long road. I mean, you can’t fix racism and discrimination in a day,” said Bond.

One more apology

Lou-ann Neel (Ika’wega), a former RBCM Indigenous collections curator who also suffered discrimination, highlighted the unprecedented nature of the event. “This would be the first time ever that a provincial agency has apologized to an Indigenous person or two people for having allowed discrimination to land on us,” Neel said.

Neel is also set to receive an apology from the institution next month. “My focus is going to actually be on pointing out to the museum their systemic barriers and to actually read them a list of things and policies and processes that failed me,” said Neel.

Now what?

As the ceremony concluded with traditional songs bringing people to the floor, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas expressed hope that the day sets a precedent for others to speak out.

“Be brave… to speak our truth… to call out injustice,” she urged.

The ceremony was about acknowledging past harm. Now, the real test for the Royal BC Museum begins: proving that an apology is just the starting line for true systemic change.

The post Royal BC Museum apologizes to Sdahl Ḵ’awaas for systemic racism in historic ceremony on Haida Gwaii appeared first on CHEK.

The post Beware scam calls using police non-emergency number, VicPD warns appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Police in Victoria are issuing a warning about suspicious phone calls appearing to come from the department’s non-emergency number, including calls in which someone impersonates an RCMP officer.

VicPD said in a news release Tuesday that it has received several new reports of spoofed calls and dropped calls involving its non-emergency number, 250-995-7654.

The complaints have come from across Canada, with some recipients reporting that the caller claimed to be an RCMP officer, even though VicPD is a municipal police force.

In one instance, the caller reportedly knew the recipient’s first and last name.

The department has previously warned the public about similar scam calls back in July.

Phone number “spoofing” allows scammers to disguise their caller ID information, making a call appear to originate from a legitimate organization.

VicPD is reminding residents never to provide personal or financial information to callers who seem suspicious, send them money or purchase gift cards for them, and should instead hang up the call immediately.

If you have given out personal or financial information, police say you should call your bank or financial institution using a trusted phone number.

VicPD says anyone who wants to verify whether a call is genuinely from the police should call the department’s non-emergency line directly and ask to be connected to the officer.

Police are also encouraging residents to share the warning with friends and family members who may be more vulnerable to scams. Suspected fraud can be reported to local police or the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

VicPD says it’s investigating the reports and asks anyone with information to contact the non-emergency line referencing file number 26-48424.

]]> 1361992 Federal government spending up $331.6 billion under Carney, budget watchdog says https://cheknews.ca/federal-government-spending-up-331-6-billion-under-carney-budget-watchdog-says-1361984/ Tue, 17 Nov 2026 20:55:49 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361984

The parliamentary budget officer is questioning the federal government's vow to spend less and invest more.

The post Federal government spending up $331.6 billion under Carney, budget watchdog says appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The parliamentary budget officer is questioning the federal government’s vow to spend less and invest more.

In a series of reports released Tuesday scrutinizing the federal budget, PBO Annette Ryan said the Liberal government’s overall fiscal situation is a bit rosier than the forecast in Ottawa’s last spending update in April.

Improved revenues from better-than-expected economic results and a tailwind of tax dollars from higher global oil prices have improved the government’s bottom line since the spring.

But Ryan said Ottawa has used up 96 per cent of that new fiscal room through fresh spending commitments, instead of meaningfully reducing the deficit.

The PBO projects the cost of federal measures is $331.6 billion higher in the three spending plans tabled so far under Prime Minister Mark Carney.

Some 60 per cent of that spending is reserved for the day-to-day operations of government, the PBO points out — not for the kind of capital spending Carney has promised to prioritize.

“The government promised to spend less to invest more. This budget spends more, invests more and borrows more,” Ryan said in a media statement on Tuesday.

John Fragos, spokesperson for Finance Minster Francois-Philippe Champagne, said of the roughly $150 billion announced in Budget 2026 for new measures, about $90 billion is focused on capital expenditure.

The PBO also acknowledged in Tuesday’s report that the Nov. 5 budget shifts Ottawa’s spending priorities toward capital.

“Even so, most new measures from Budget 2025 onward have gone to day-to-day operations,” the report read.

Fragos said instances in the budget of the government borrowing beyond its means are focused solely on generating future growth and setting the stage for greater investments in Canada.

He also pointed to the government’s fiscal anchors — a declining deficit-to-GDP ratio and a pledge to balance the operating budget — as proof of prudent financial management.

The debt-to-GDP ratio — a fiscal anchor for past Liberal governments — is also on a lower trajectory in Budget 2026.

While the government laid out a path to meet its fiscal anchors in this year’s budget, the PBO warned Tuesday that those margins are narrow.

The PBO says if the deficit is $2 billion higher than Ottawa expects in the next fiscal year, the government will fail to fulfil its pledge to reduce the deficit as a share of the economy.

Ryan has raised concerns about how the government defines capital versus operating spending. That definition matters a lot when determining whether the government is meeting its other fiscal anchor — balancing the operating budget.

In Tuesday’s report, Ryan argued that if the government used more internationally accepted definitions for capital and operating spending, Ottawa would fail to balance its operating budget over the forecast horizon.

“Whether the anchor is met depends on how capital is defined,” the report said.

Ryan’s analysis also attempts to get a sense of the scope of government borrowing beyond the deficit line.

Her report says that total borrowing outlined in Budget 2026 is expected to reach $765 billion over five years — $476 billion more than the cumulative deficit of $289 billion.

Total borrowing includes loans to Crown corporations and the purchase of assets — much of that debt does not appear directly on Ottawa’s balance sheets. Capital investments like military equipment are considered assets and show up in the deficit over time as they depreciate, even though they’re paid for upfront.

In other words, taking out a loan to buy a car might leave you with an asset, but that doesn’t mean you’re not still paying off the loan and interest costs.

The government will have to find that $765 billion whether it adds to the deficit or not — and the PBO notes that the recent Bank of Canada interest rate hike is set to increase borrowing costs for Canadians and governments alike.

Public debt costs are now the fastest-growing line item on a year-over-year basis in the federal budget, Ryan noted during an appearance at the House of Commons’ finance committee on Tuesday. Those costs are expected to become larger than the cost of federal health transfers to provinces in the years to come.

When a government’s spending outpaces revenues, that means taking on debt and pushing the need to cover those costs into the future, Ryan said.

Some of those borrowing costs are paid back through interest on loaned money or returns on investments. But loans can go bad and projects might flounder, so those returns are not guaranteed.

Scientists are recording unprecedented ocean temperatures off Vancouver Island, with some areas warming as much as 2.5°C above normal, raising concerns about potential impacts on marine ecosystems.

Ocean Networks Canada (ONC), a University of Victoria initiative, says the unusually warm conditions are being detected hundreds of metres below the ocean’s surface, signalling the arrival of El Niño impacts along B.C.’s Pacific coastline.

On Nov. 8, a record-high temperature of 8.21°C was recorded at the Barkley Canyon Upper Slope monitoring site, located 400 metres below the surface off Vancouver Island.

That temperature was 2.49°C above the site’s long-term average and nearly 0.9°C warmer than the previous record set in 2019. Monitoring at the site began in 2009.

Temperatures remain elevated in mid-November, sitting about 1.6°C above normal.

“What makes these observations important is that we’re seeing significant warming not just at the surface, but hundreds of metres below it,” said Jay Cullen, ONC’s interim president and chief executive, in a release.

“We will be monitoring these conditions closely over the coming months, as warmer ocean temperatures can have important implications for marine ecosystems and ocean health.”

The warming is also being detected at the Clayoquot Slope monitoring site, more than 1,200 metres below the surface.

Since late summer, several of ONC’s deep-sea monitoring stations have recorded their warmest seasonal temperatures on record. The exception is the deepest site, Cascadia Basin, at 2,650 metres, where temperatures remain within normal ranges.

Warmer-than-average conditions are also being observed closer to shore in the Strait of Georgia, where temperatures have remained unusually high throughout 2026.

ONC scientists warn that additional warming associated with El Niño could put further stress on marine ecosystems already experiencing elevated temperatures.

“Since the start of 2026, the VENUS observatory has shown temperatures consistently higher than we’ve previously observed. And this was before any El Niño effects started to appear,” said ONC science director Jordan Watson.

RELATED: Super El Niño to follow extremely dry October on Vancouver Island

Watson said the combined warming is particularly concerning for a region that supports migrating salmon, spawning herring and marine mammals.

He said understanding the potential impacts is critical for protecting ecosystems that support B.C.’s fisheries, tourism and coastal communities.

ONC operates two major underwater observatories off B.C.’s coast, including the 850-kilometre NEPTUNE network offshore Vancouver Island and the VENUS observatory in the Salish Sea.

Scientists will continue monitoring ocean temperatures and other conditions in the coming months to understand the potential impacts on marine life better.

The future of the Oak Bay Marina is starting to take shape after the District of Oak Bay announced it had chosen a proponent to negotiate the water lease of the marina with.

The District of Oak Bay has chosen the Oak Bay Marine Group (OBMG) to begin negotiations with for the marina lease, which is set to expire at the end of next year.

OBMG was one of two groups that had submitted a proposal to operate the marina, with the other being Xhamasung Holdings, a jointly owned economic development partnership between Songhees Nation and Esquimalt Nation (Xwsepsum).

RELATED: Two groups pitch future of Oak Bay Marina as lease expiry nears

The municipality says it chose OBMG over Xhamasung Holdings based on an independent evaluation of both proposals.

The evaluation took into consideration criteria that Oak Bay council had established for the marina site – with the financial category weighted the highest at 40 per cent, followed by operational (30 per cent), community (20 per cent) and environmental (10 per cent).

While the district has chosen OBMG to negotiate a new long-term lease with, it notes that a final agreement is still subject to negotiations, followed by approval from Oak Bay council.

“Prior to entering into any lease agreement, the District will publicly disclose the proposed lease terms,” said the municipality on Tuesday. 

The district notes that the lease is for the water portion of the marina and does not include the restaurant/coffee shop building nor the remainder of the site. Those areas are currently under discussion, says the municipality.

“Council looks forward to engaging with all interested parties on the future of those remaining portions of the Turkey Head (Spewhung Point) site,” said the district.

The current lease at the Oak Bay Marina is set to expire in December 2027. It comes after a long-term lease between the district and the OBMG, which had operated the marina since 1962, expired in 2022. Afterwards, the district granted the marine group a five-year short-term lease to give the municipality time to develop a long-term vision for the property.

“Council recognizes and appreciates the interest, effort, and contributions of both proponents throughout the process and the important role each has played in informing discussions about the future marina operations,” said the municipality Tuesday.
